item: Auth: session-authorised set-password and real email for provider accounts

closes.finding: A30 (2026-09-08): an account created by ATProto sign-in can never acquire a second sign-in method, and the unlink refusal's own remedy is unreachable
closes.ruling: owner ruled session-authorised set-password + real email

not_lab_observed.statement: code-only slice: no PDS, no browser, no containers. The proof is unit and integration tests plus CI.
rerun_must_prove: a real authorization server's consent screen and callback carry the step_up purpose through unchanged
the assertion spends against a real Postgres step_up_tokens row (these tests use an in-memory fake mirroring the SQL predicate, not the SQL)
the settings prompt appears for the account A30 created, and disappears once both steps are done
after setting a password: a password login succeeds and the last-method unlink returns 204 against the live instance
the email change from the placeholder delivers its confirmation to the new mailbox and no bounce is generated for the old one
not_lab_observed.still_unverified_unchanged: the PRODUCTION hosted-client OAuth path (client-metadata.json fetched by the auth server over https) — a loopback lab cannot mint that origin

step_up_contract.state: the SAME signed httpOnly 10-minute state cookie, with purpose=step_up plus uid and sid INSIDE the signed payload
step_up_contract.verification: VerifyAssertion factored OUT of Complete/CompleteAuth and called by both, so login and step-up cannot drift one check apart (iss RFC 9207, code exchange, sub, scope / JWKS + nonce)
step_up_contract.subject_binding: SubjectLinkedTo — the attested subject must belong to the bound account
step_up_contract.grant: ?step_up=<raw token> on return_to; NO session cookie is minted

token.storage: hex SHA-256 in step_up_tokens (raw never persisted)
token.supersede: a new challenge deletes the session's previous unspent token
token.housekeeping: expired rows swept opportunistically at mint time; no new cron
token.why_a_row_not_a_jwt: single use and statelessness are incompatible — the consume is ONE statement whose predicate carries the owning account, the owning session, used_at IS NULL and an unexpired expires_at
token.why_the_query_string: the token authorises nothing in any other browser, so whoever can read this history already holds the session it is useless without; the settings page still strips it with history.replaceState

routes_added.POST /api/v1/auth/step-up/start: begin a step-up with a linked provider
routes_added.POST /api/v1/auth/me/password/set: set a FIRST password; separate route so the change route keeps required:[current_password,new_password] and this one has no such field at all

routes_changed.POST /api/v1/auth/me/email-change: accepts step_up_token in place of current_password for a passwordless account; exactly one of the two, both is 422
routes_changed.DELETE /api/v1/me/oauth-identities/{prov: the last-method 422 now names /api/v1/auth/me/password/set instead of the unreachable reset flow
routes_changed.POST /api/v1/auth/me/password: the no-password 409 names the same reachable route

mail_promises.password_set_notice: ATTEMPTED, best-effort, to the account address — on an account still holding its placeholder it CANNOT be delivered. Attempted rather than skipped because the address may already have been moved; the UI never claims it was sent
mail_promises.email_change_confirmation: unchanged and MUST-DELIVER, to the NEW address only. The step-up replaces the 'are you the account holder' half, never mailbox possession. The route still refuses to start with no mail path (mail_not_configured)
mail_promises.email_change_old_address_notice: SKIPPED when the old address is the unroutable placeholder (.invalid TLD) — there is no old mailbox to warn. Keyed on undeliverability, not on 'this account used a provider': a real old address still gets its notice (both directions tested)

negatives.attempt: anonymous step-up start or password set
step-up with a provider the account has not linked
set a password on an account that has one
negatives.answer: 422 password_already_set, checked BEFORE the token is spent

negatives.attempt: no token / unknown / already spent / expired
a token from another session of the SAME account
email change with a step-up on a password account
callback whose subject is linked to a different account
new address resolving to another account's email OR username
negatives.answer: 409 email_taken — the step-up authorises WHO, never WHAT
unchanged — the second factor is a LOGIN challenge and the step-up runs through that same login

migration.rename_reason: the federation follow-ups merged first and took 0143 (0143_validator_safe_channel_handles). A gap is not an escape: internal/dbmigrate TestEmbeddedSourceExposesEveryVersion refuses a GAP as firmly as a duplicate, so the only correct response to losing the race is the rename — a number a branch reserves is not reserved until it merges

applied_for_real.cluster: native Postgres 16.15 on 127.0.0.1:55444, initdb'd EMPTY (no reused volume)
applied_for_real.run: go run ./cmd/api migrate up, from_version 0 -> to_version 144 in one pass
applied_for_real.table: step_up_tokens with 8 columns and 4 indexes (_pkey, _token_hash_idx UNIQUE, _user_id_idx, _expires_at_idx)
applied_for_real.reversible: the .down.sql drops it cleanly and the .up.sql re-creates it identically — what makes a rollback a tag flip rather than a restore

vidra-core.make ci: PASS (fmt-check, vet, migrate-lint 144 up migrations, openapi-verify, sqlc-verify, test-race) — re-run after the rebase onto main and the 0143->0144 rename
PASS, exit 0 — re-run after the rebase
new_tests: internal/auth/stepup_fake_test.go (in-memory step_up_tokens mirroring the SQL predicate)
vidra-core.tagged integration lane EXECUTED: go test -tags=integration -race -p 1 -count=1 ./internal/store/... ./internal/auth/... ./internal/httpapi/... against the empty-migrated native cluster above plus a native Redis on 127.0.0.1:56399: store ok 6.6s, auth ok 10.6s, httpapi ok 59.1s. -p 1 because those packages share one database and would otherwise race each other's fixtures rather than the code

vidra-user.regen: lib/api/generated.ts regenerated from the core branch's api/openapi.yaml — the user PR stays DRAFT until core merges, because contract-ci regenerates from core's DEFAULT branch
vidra-user.fixture_discipline: the User and OAuthIdentity fixtures are typed FROM the regenerated contract, so a field leaving the schema stops the test compiling rather than letting it pass on a fiction

gates.vidra (meta): evidence only; python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p '*_test.py'

frontend_surface.placement: first card on /settings/security, rendered ONLY when has_password is false or email_placeholder is true
frontend_surface.copy: states the consequence — losing the Bluesky/OIDC account loses this one, and the generated address means no reset link has anywhere to go
frontend_surface.landing_params: read SERVER-side from searchParams and passed as props (the pattern app/login/page.tsx uses for ?oauth_error) — a client component scraping window.location in an effect would be a hydration mismatch and a synchronous setState in an effect
frontend_surface.session_discipline: the linked-identities read goes through useSettledSession and is additionally gated on the card applying at all, so an account with nothing to fix spends no request
frontend_surface.url_hygiene: history.replaceState strips step_up / step_up_error / secure on mount

open: a step-up assertion is bound to a session but NOT to the action it was collected for: the token that unlocks the password form would also unlock the email form. Both are steps the same person just authorised, so this is a scope choice rather than a hole — recorded because it is not obvious from the routes
no audit event records WHICH provider a refused step-up was attempted with beyond the reason code; auth.step_up.grant carries the provider only on success
the placeholder predicate keys on the .invalid TLD, so an operator who configures a different unroutable domain for provider accounts would not get the old-address-notice suppression
